newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ten Network says govt ruling removes uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Ten Network says govt ruling removes uncertainty.

text.p: Television broadcaster Ten Network Ltd said on Friday that a ruling by the government that major shareholder CanWest Global Communications Corp should cut its stake to 57.5 percent would help remove uncertainty surrounding the company.

"This decision contributes to an orderly resolution of the issues involved in the shareholding structure of Network Ten and has therefore helped remove some of the uncertainty over future regulatory policy toward the network," Ten chairman John Studdy said in a statement.

Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said earlier CanWest's 76 percent economic interest in Ten Group Ltd was inconsistent with foreign investment policy and that he had ordered it to sell down its stake to a previously sanctioned 57.5 percent.
"We will continue to work with the government and Australian Broadcasting Authority to ensure a final result that strengthens Network Ten, its investors and its future," Studdy said.
Costello said shares held in Ten by CanWest associates Selli Pty Ltd, Numeration Pty Ltd, Turnand Pty Ltd and Donholken Pty Ltd would need to be sold by September 30, irrespective of price.

The Treasurer said this would have the effect of returning CanWest's holding to its level of November 1995 when the Australian Broadcasting Authority, the industry's regulatory body, ruled that CanWest did not control Ten even though it held an economic interest of 57.5 percent.

Under Australian regulations, foreign investors may not control or hold no more than a 15 percent voting interest in an Australian broadcaster and total foreign holding must not exceed 20 percent. CanWest says it meets this requirement by voting only 15 percent of its stake in the unlisted broadcaster.
